rows.summary: Owner decisions recorded: D-003 option 2 (python-docx + fpdf2), D-005 option 1 (extractive research), D-006 option 1. For D-006, the owner preferred option 2 on their Claude subscription only if allowed; the Consumer Terms forbid using the Services to train models and forbid scripted access without an API key. D-002 stays open: the chosen Google Programmable Search JSON API is closed to new customers and ends on 2027-01-01; options revised.

Dashboard Development tab shows a "Project status" section parsed from this file (snapshot, model table, model-related open items, recent model work); the build now reads real-inference verification from the model table instead of a hard-coded list. New idle-machine benchmark of the current bundles: ML-001 v2.1.0 (ONNX) 391 ms mean per request, peak process memory 481 MB (budget < 550 MB); ML-002 v1.1.0 3.1 ms per pair.

Installed and verified ML-001 v2.1.0 (user's Kaggle re-export of the v2.0.0 weights to ONNX, no retraining). SHA-256 verified; every Kaggle metric identical to v2.0.0 (precision 0.851); ONNX parity 3.8e-5. Laptop, full test set through the app's ONNX path: precision 0.828, 456 ms mean latency, RSS 426 MB after load and 486 MB peak (budget < 550 MB), no PyTorch; 200/200 suggestions identical to v2.0.0 PyTorch. Wrote title-expander-2.1.0.md; model card, registry (Verified) and spec (memory budget approved via PR #40) updated. The skills defect remains.

D-012 delivery: claude.ai's GitHub entry is an integration, not a callable connector, so the dashboard is kept current by the cloud scheduled task "Findrr dashboard sync" (fires on PRs merged into main; uploads only changed dashboard files). Hand-tested: 34 s, all writes succeeded. Trigger configured in the claude.ai form by the owner; this PR's merge is its first live test.

D-011 and D-012 (owner decisions): added scripts/model_dashboard/, the source and data of the Findrr Model Observatory dashboard: page.html, dashboard.json, bench.py, build.py, committed data/, and a pre-commit hook that rebuilds and stages data/ before each commit (never blocks; no-op without the bundles). Decisions are parsed from this log. Not part of the app; real CPU inference only, no training. Laptop benchmark on an idle machine (before PR #37): ML-001 mean 611 ms per request (budget 1,500), ML-002 5.7 ms per pair (budget 50). A run on a saturated machine (load 13) was discarded; bench.py now refuses to save busy runs. The build follows the registry: after PR #40 it shows ML-001 v2.1.0 awaiting its Kaggle run, with metrics from v2.0.0. Hook not yet installed (git config core.hooksPath scripts/model_dashboard/hooks); GitHub connector for live reads not yet connected.

D-004 resolved by the user: option 1, ONNX fp32 with a KV cache. New t5_onnx_decoding (NumPy beam search, shared with the notebook) and t5_onnx_export (decoder step written against the weights, parity-checked). TitleExpanderRunner no longer uses PyTorch. ML-001 v2.1.0 registry entry. Notebook 01 exports and evaluates the ONNX files, and can reuse an accepted v2.0.0 bundle without retraining. Local evidence on the v2.0.0 weights: logit difference 3.8e-5, 200/200 outputs identical to PyTorch, 435 MB after load, peak 486 MB over 400 requests (was 994–1,248 MB). Found: skills can pull ML-001 off-topic. Opened PR #40 (user review).

Installed ML-002 v1.1.0 and ML-001 v2.0.0 (run 5) bundles; both pass acceptance and real inference is verified. Local full test-set re-evaluation through the app runners: ML-001 precision 0.828 (Kaggle 0.851; the runner drops the input title), 407 ms; ML-002 identical to Kaggle, 2.8 ms per pair. PR #37 (self-merged): the ML-002 tokenizer no longer pulls in PyTorch, 659 → 119 MB with identical scores. Wrote evaluation reports and model cards and marked both models Verified in the registry. A local ML-001 ONNX prototype gives identical outputs at 531 MB; INT8 variants fall to 0.685–0.728. D-004 updated with the evidence.

D-010 option 1 implemented: up to 30 O*NET job titles per occupation as training-only inputs (train 42,624 examples, 22,967 input titles; val/test unchanged, no overlap), 15 epochs, repetition penalty off (runner reads it from preprocess_config.json), training-sample precision reported. 193 tests pass.

D-010 revised with local inference on the run-4 bundle (500 inputs): penalty off 0.591, 4 beams 0.568, first-title occupation lock 0.635, training inputs 0.727. The model under-fits; decoding changes cannot reach 0.75. Found the bundle's threshold edited to 0.0.

ML-001 Kaggle run 4 (user, input-title split): occupation precision 0.603 (target 0.75) failed. Local analysis: repetition_penalty=1.2 penalises shared words, and 97% of gold outputs repeat a word across titles; the constraint already prevents repeats. Raised D-010.

D-009 resolved by the user: option 1. Notebook 01 now splits by input title (hashed per normalised anchor; no wording crosses splits; every occupation trained on). Local data prep: 21,304/2,720/2,525 examples, no anchor overlap, test occupations all in training; broad-group baseline 0.732, same-detailed-SOC 0.929. Reports precision on never-seen wording (110 examples). 192 tests pass.

ML-001 Kaggle run 3 (user, with the PR #31 fix): occupation precision 0.478 (target 0.75) failed; valid ratio 1.0, repetition 0.0001 and AC-ML-001.1 5 passed. Local analysis: the occupation-disjoint split means only 17.5% of test reference titles were ever training targets, and the 0.736 baseline behind the 0.75 threshold wrongly included the test occupations' own titles; the fair broad-group baseline is 0.579. Raised D-009.
